spec.subject: 📌 START HERE — What is GRAVITY? (The Specification, v3)
spec.body:
Pinned · Methodology

GRAVITY stands for Game-Rate Adjusted Value, Impact, Talent, and Yield. It estimates a player's per-minute quality and adjusts for role, availability, and documented injury risk — measuring not just how good a player is, but how much of that ability a team actually receives.

In plain terms: GRAVITY = (how good per minute) × (how reliably he's on the floor), graded against the whole league by the same formula. No reputation inputs, no external rankings — the judgment lives in the formula, which is published in full and applied identically to all 644 players.
THE SCALE
  50   league-average minute
  60+  quality starter
  80+  franchise engine
  97.8 Nikola Jokić (2025-26 max)

Version history

v1.0 · Jul 10 initial 644-player ranking  →  v2 · Jul 10 Butler ACL correction (#13→#58)  →  v3 · Jul 10 CTG filtered on/off integrated

House rule for reading anything here: green is the model speaking, amber is the model betting, grey is the world providing context.

The full mathematics — every equation, weight, shrinkage rule, tier cut, and the complete injury-override table — is published as a standalone technical document, typeset like everything else here.

Save spec.pdf
GRAVITY · The Gravity Report · thegravityreport.com · est. July 2026

ed30.subject: NEW — The 30: every team, one number (July 2026)
ed30.body:
New database view · 30 teams · Team GRAVITY

Team GRAVITY is the expected force of one minute of a team's floor time, built from a fixed 240-minute game. Every roster spot supplies the minutes a team can actually count on (a two-season blend; draft-slot priors for rookies); minutes nobody on the roster can cover are priced at replacement force 35.0. Because availability enters through minutes, a fragile star is priced once — never twice. Teams land on the same scale as players: 50 is a league-average minute.

TOP 10 — JULY 2026 · official rosters, Jul 29
  1  Thunder    OKC  55.1      6  Rockets   HOU  50.6
  2  Knicks     NYK  52.4      7  Sixers    PHI  50.4
  3  Spurs      SAS  52.0      8  Magic     ORL  50.3
  4  Nuggets    DEN  51.5      9  Wolves    MIN  50.2
  5  Celtics    BOS  50.6     10  Pistons   DET  49.8

The table shows what the average hides: starters vs bench force, how much of each team's value sits in its top three players, and how many minutes each roster still can't cover. Click any team for its full 240-minute allocation.

Two honesty notes. Unsigned is unsigned: free agents — restricted ones included — are nobody's minutes yet, so Cleveland is priced without Harden, Detroit without Duren, Sacramento without DeRozan. Those holes show up as replacement-priced fill, and the All-Star edition re-prices whatever has been signed by then. And one trade doesn't exist yet: the agreed Leonard–Ingram swap is unconsummated while the league's investigation runs, so Kawhi is a Clipper here and Toronto keeps Ingram. Official rosters only.

Registered forecast E1: P ≈ 75% that The 30 predicts the 2026-27 standings to Spearman ρ ≥ 0.60 (final regular-season wins). ρ ≥ 0.60 = win · 0.50–0.60 = near miss · below 0.50 = miss. For calibration: weighted by who actually played the minutes, team force explained the 2025-26 win column at ρ = 0.963 — the forward number prices roster churn, injuries, and our own minute-projection errors. Scored in Forecast Audit №1, July 2027.
In plain terms: a talent ranking of rosters, weighted by playing time, honest about its depth charts — and on the record about how well it should track the standings.

kawhi.subject: The Kawhi Anomaly — the biggest rebound ever recorded by a 34-year-old
kawhi.body:
Article №4 · Preseason 2026–27 · the ballot winner

Kawhi Leonard went from a good starter to the fifth-best player in the league per minute, at 34. That jump is the biggest one-year gain ever recorded by a player his age. Late surges usually fade. This article asks which half of his will last.

  • Two records: the biggest one-year jump ever by a player 34 or older, and the only star since 1978 to set career highs in usage and true shooting in the same season after 33.
  • Late surges fade: eight players surged to star level after 31. None kept three-quarters of the improvement the next season.
  • Two kinds of improvement: his bigger role usually lasts; his hot shooting usually doesn't.
  • The forecast: rebuilt piece by piece, we predict an impact of +1.31 next season, roughly a top-ten level.

Registered forecasts: top 8 in The 644 (July 2027) 50% · top 8 in Box Plus/Minus 30% · usage stays at 30% or more 60% · true shooting falls below .610 65%.

Open the article (PDF) Save kawhi.pdf
Built on GRAVITY Retrospective, run over every season since 1977–78.

queta.subject: The Queta Problem — why he’s a top-50 player, and why 2026-27 proves it (rev. v2)
queta.rev: Oct 6 2026 — relabeled: an article typeset in LaTeX, not a research paper; no content changes. Earlier: v2, Jul 11 2026, after external review — model output separated from editorial scenario weights (each weight now anchored to an observable rate); on/off language corrected to cross-season persistence, and the shrunk-input counterfactual re-run properly: #53–55, not ≈#48 (the harshest reading grazes the claim); comparables disclosed as 33 seasons / 22 players (32% per-player rate) + cutoff-sensitivity table; grading tightened: #51–70 = near miss, not push. The registered 75% is unchanged — that is the bet. Then Jul 31 2026 — working-paper status labels added to every page (PDF footer + status notice, also on the web edition); no findings or numbers changed.
queta.body:
№ 41 · Trust the data — a registered forecast · revised v2

Our ranking put Neemias Queta — twice waived, 39th pick — at 58.8 · #41 · T4, a full tier above his reputation. Instead of defending the number, this note attacks it twice, keeps what survives, and converts it into a registered bet.

  • The anti-fluke chart: his season workload grew nearly 6× (333 → 1,926 minutes) and his efficiency went up — PSA 130 → 132 → 134, with a 97th-percentile playoff series shown separately.
  • Stress test I: only ~⅓ of on/off persists year to year (r = 0.317, n = 184). Discounted uniformly, #41 doesn't move; discount his number alone — the harshest reading — and he lands #53–55, just outside. The bet never rested on the shiny number, and v2 owes you that it grazes the claim.
  • Stress test II: 33 comparable big-man seasons from 22 players since 2020 (the Gobert / Robert Williams / Jarrett Allen family): 39% by season, 32% by player, delivered a top-50-caliber follow-up — robust to every cutoff we varied.
  • The market agrees: Boston signed Mitchell Robinson July 6 — then extended Queta for $56M anyway.
Registered forecast: we assign P(top-50 in July 2027) ≈ 75% · P(top-25) ≈ 40% — GRAVITY prices the scenarios, the weights are ours, and the article shows the anchors. Falsification on the record: #50+ = win · #51–70 = near miss (a failure owing a diagnosis) · below #70 = clean miss.
In plain terms: it's not a moonshot claim — it just requires this season to mostly repeat. We wrote down in advance exactly what counts as being wrong, and #51 counts.
Open the article (PDF) Save queta.pdf
Implications for GRAVITY: + empirical on/off persistence (r = 0.317) is now a candidate model input.

morant.subject: The Rise and Fall of Ja Morant — a statistical account, 2017–2026 (rev. v2)
morant.rev: Oct 6 2026 — relabeled: an article typeset in LaTeX, not a research paper; no content changes. Earlier: v2, Jul 11 2026, after external review — absence ledger corrected (the shoulder cost 48 games, not 73; 79 of 246 = 32.1%), inference language tightened, forward scenarios → availability × impact matrix, sensitivity appendix added (#112–#147 across all variations). Full note on the last page. The errors were ours. Then Jul 31 2026 — working-paper status labels added to every page (PDF footer + status notice, also on the web edition); no findings or numbers changed.
morant.body:
№ 140 · The steepest fall — a career autopsy · revised v2

Seven seasons, one instrument: from unranked recruit to the 97th percentile of the league (2021-22), then an availability catastrophe — 79 of 246 games since 2023 — and one 569-minute season the data cannot fully judge.

  • Missing, not choosing: of his eFG collapse, 88% was shot-making, only 0.7 points of it shot-selection (exact Shapley split over shot zones — what zone data can't see is scoped in §6.2).
  • The sample-size problem: the three-point collapse covers 20-of-85; its Wilson interval [.158, .336] contains his career norm — too few attempts to tell decline from variance.
  • The touch paradox: the only split that moved beyond doubt was his free throw — upward, to .897.
  • What the draft model missed: his college assist rate was +3.5σ against the 2026 cohort — the skill the formula didn't count is the one that survived everything.
  • New in v2 — the stress test: every model variation tested (overrides off, equal season weights, different anchors, reliability stack deleted) lands him #112–#147. The number isn't an artifact of any single judgment call.
In plain terms: #140 is a defensible price for the delivery risk. It is probably the wrong forecast of the talent. Both statements are the same mathematics, read in two directions.
Open the article (PDF) Save morant.pdf
rev. v2, Jul 11 2026, following external review: absence ledger corrected (the shoulder cost 48 games, not 73 — the other 25 were the suspension; denominator 246, not 249), inference language tightened to what the intervals support, forward scenarios replaced by an availability × impact matrix, sensitivity appendix added. The errors were ours; the full revision note is on the article's last page.
Implications for GRAVITY: + creation added to the rookie blend · + zone mix ≠ shot difficulty · + CIs before adjectives.

welcome.subject: Why this looks like 1999 (read once, then archive)
welcome.body:
About this publication

Articles are letters: numbered, dated, permanent, addressed to anyone who takes basketball arguments seriously. An inbox is the honest interface for that — nothing trends, nothing autoplays, the archive is the product.

Each note ships three ways: the PDF proves depth, the web version gets read, the thread gets discovered. The Ledger keeps us honest and the Audit grades us annually.

Subscribe by RSS (feed.xml) — the email edition is coming.

In plain terms: an institution, not a feed. Slower on purpose.
GRAVITY · How good, times how often.

draft_duren.subject: №3 (in progress) — Duren: the best traditional center is 22
draft_duren.body:
Draft · in progress · confirmed Jul 31 2026

GRAVITY already believes it: Jalen Duren sits #14 of 644 — a traditional center inside the top 15 that no consensus board has. He is also already part of this publication's evidence: Article №2's comparables table lists his 2024–25 season as the cohort's best follow-up (+1.02 → +1.60, 97th percentile). №3 extends published machinery — silhouette, base rates, shrinks, and a registered bet with an audit date.

Confirmed by the editorial desk with the ballot at 0–0. The ballot below now decides №4.

draft_no4.subject: №4 (ballot closed) — Kawhi won; Jokić and Flagg are being written too
draft_no4.body:
Ballot closed · Kawhi won

The ballot is closed. Kawhi won it, and №4, The Kawhi Anomaly, is in the Inbox. №3 (Duren) is in progress, and the Jokić and Flagg articles are being written too.

The Kawhi Anomaly: top-8 in 2027?
Published October 6 as Article №4 — see the Inbox.

Jokić: still the best, and 2027 proves it.
GRAVITY #1 by 4.9 points (97.8 vs 92.9) — yet two straight MVPs went elsewhere. The article would quantify the voter-vs-data gap and the aging math for why a 31-year-old repeats at #1.

Flagg: top-10 in year two?
Rookie of the Year at 19 (21.0 / 6.7 / 4.5), and the rookie module was built for exactly this question: how often does a season like that become top-10 by year two? The bet would grade against the July 2027 edition.

Final result: Kawhi won the ballot.

del_butler.subject: ♻️ RECALLED — Jimmy Butler at #13 (v1)
del_butler.body:
Deleted Items · kept visible on purpose

RECALLED  The sender recalled this ranking on Jul 10, 2026.

Reason: the model rated 38 games of elite per-minute play as "availability risk." It didn't know the season ended with a torn ACL on Jan 19. With the same injury discount every rehab case gets, Butler moved #13 → #58, and the correction shipped the same day, in public.

In plain terms: the trash folder is part of the methodology. Errors get corrected in public and kept on display — that's what makes the wins believable.
